changes.source_excerpt: 2.2 For small $h$ with $x+h\in W$, put $\Delta(t)=\Phi(t,x+h)-\Phi(t,x)$, $S_h(t)=S(t,x+h)$, and $A_h(t)=Df(\Phi(t,x+h))$. The uniform remainder in [F1] gives $\Delta=S h+o(\|h\|_2)$ uniformly on $J$. On each segment between $\Phi(t,x)$ and $\Phi(t,x+h)$, the chain rule [F7] and [F6] applied coordinatewise to $Df$ give $ A_h-A=\int_0^1 D^2f(\Phi+s\Delta)[\Delta,\cdot] ds. $ Uniform continuity of $D^2f$ on $K$ [F3] and $\Delta=S h+o(\|h\|)$ therefore imply $A_h-A=D^2f(\Phi)[S h,\cdot]+o(\|h\|_2)$ uniformly in $t$. [F1, F3, F6, F7, step 1.1, algebra]
changes.proposed_replacement: 2.2 For small $h$ with $x+h\in W$, put $\Delta(t)=\Phi(t,x+h)-\Phi(t,x)$, $S_h(t)=S(t,x+h)$, and $A_h(t)=Df(\Phi(t,x+h))$. The uniform remainder in [F1] gives $\Delta=S h+o(\|h\|_2)$ uniformly on $[0,T_+]$. On each segment between $\Phi(t,x)$ and $\Phi(t,x+h)$, the chain rule [F7] and [F6] applied coordinatewise to $Df$ give $ A_h-A=\int_0^1 D^2f(\Phi+s\Delta)[\Delta,\cdot] ds. $ Uniform continuity of $D^2f$ on $K$ [F3] and $\Delta=S h+o(\|h\|)$ therefore imply $A_h-A=D^2f(\Phi)[S h,\cdot]+o(\|h\|_2)$ uniformly in $t$. [F1, F3, F6, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

changes.source_excerpt: 4.1 If $x_j\to x$, [F1] gives uniform convergence of $\Phi(\cdot,x_j)$ and $S(\cdot,x_j)$ on $J$. Continuity of $D^2f$ on $K$ then gives uniform convergence of the coefficients and forcing in the linear equations for $H_h$; subtracting their integral equations and applying [F5] proves $H_h(\cdot,x_j)\to H_h(\cdot,x)$ uniformly. Thus the second state derivative is continuous in $(t,x)$. [F1, F3, F5, F6, step 2.1, step 3.1]
changes.proposed_replacement: 4.1 If $x_j\to x$, [F1] gives uniform convergence of $\Phi(\cdot,x_j)$ and $S(\cdot,x_j)$ on $[0,T_+]$. Thus the second state derivative is continuous in $(t,x)$. [F1, F3, F5, F6, step 2.1, step 3.1]
